text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Cricket captain Mark Taylor turned down an offer by umpire David Shepard to leave the ground because of poor light, allowing Australia to move from 0-18 after eight overs to 2-77 at stumps against the West Indies in the Second Test at the Sydney Cricket Ground. Page 25.

Weekend speculation that talks had taken place between News Corp chief executive and chairman Rupert Murdoch and Channel Nine boss Kerry Packer, with a view to a compromise over the rugby league war in Australia, have been quashed by Australian Rugby League chairman Ken Arthurson who said he had no knowledge of compromise talks talking place between the two. Page 25.

The Wollongong City Wolves have retained their place in the top six in the Erricson Cup National Soccer League after drawing 1-1 with UTS Olympic at Belmore Sports Ground last night, mainly due to the efforts of goal-keeper Brett Hughes who pulled off three amazing saves. Page 29.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Sydney Cricket Ground is somewhat the worse for wear much to the disappointment of those playing the Second Test, and not all of the problems can be attributed to Michael Jackson concerts and football games. The grounds have become open to use from all sectors of the community so that the pitch does not have time to recover from each assault. Page 25.
Australian Peter Senior beat Greg Norman at his own game yesterday in the Greg Norman Holden Classic tournament at Royal Melbourne, finishing seven under the card, one below Norman. Page 27.

SOCOG, the organising committee for the Sydney Olympic Games, and the Rushcutters Bay Maritime Reserve Trust have been put under pressure by Australian Yachting Federation president Bruce Dickson who is pushing for a headquarters and coaching centre to be left as a legacy after the Games to the Australian sailing community. Page 27.
THE AGE

Leading Jockey Steven King is expected to lodge an appeal against a suspension for careless riding at Flemington yesterday before he leaves for Hong Kong to ride Count Chivas in the International Vase next Sunday. Page 2.

One week after the International Olympic Committee's medical director Prince Alexandre De Moerode said fixed bans were ineffective against the fight against drugs in sport, the IOC has urged the Australian Sports Drugs Agency not to ease up on drug cheats by shortening bans. Page 2.

Although rain halted play for a brief period, the women of the Victorian Women's Cricket Team were not deterred in their quest for a back-to-back national championship, beating Queensland on Saturday and taking their record in the series to 3-0. Page 8.
HERALD SUN
Golfer Greg Norman is expected to resume playing the Australian Masters at Huntingdale when his Greg Norman Holden Classic tournament moves to February from 1998. Page 81.

Canberra Golfer Craig Carmichael won the A$36,000 Australian PGA Trainees Championship by three strokes at the Newcastle Golf Club yesterday, after birdying two of the last three holes. Carmichael won from American Jim Schuman who shot 73 to his 74. Page 9.

The Kookaburra Australian Hockey team won 5-4 over India in New Delhi yesterday in the first of a three-Test hockey series. Captain Jay Stacy celebrated his 200th international appearance with the largely experimental team which has only three Atlanta Olympians in the team. Page 76.
DAILY TELEGRAPH

Skipper Brad Gibson and his crew on the Southern Cross won the second heat of the New South Wales 18-footer championship in rough conditions on Sydney Harbour yesterday. The Steve Quigly-steered AEI was the comeback story of the day with the crew coming from near last to take second place. Page 33.

After setting Queensland on course for its third outright Sheffield Shield win this season, pace-bowler Andrew Bichel raised the stakes in his three-year quest to make next year's Ashes tour, taking the floor and forcing Victoria to battle hard all day. Page 39.

Leading trainers Gai Waterhouse, John Hawkes and Clarrie Conners will be relying on weight of numbers to break their hoodoo, in the A$150,000 Panthers Hawkesbury Gold Cup, in a field expected to be the best ever due to the tireless efforts of the Hawkesbuy Race Club Committee in promoting the club's signature race. Page 44.
